title: Introduce dynamic primer fabric runner and hotpath attribution exporter
author: Priya Kothari
release_notes: Adds a new workload runner (primer fabric) for mixed-length warmup patterns and a hotpath attribution exporter that produces per-kernel occupancy maps and flamegraph-compatible outputs.
description:
Motivation:
This PR adds a new benchmark runner and reporting pipeline to help surface short-lived kernel occupancy and prefetch effectiveness under mixed priming patterns. Existing runners emphasize long-lived sessions or synthetic bursts; we needed a lightweight fabric that can weave short primers, mid-length continuations, and occasional long tails to exercise KV cache hotpath transitions and prefetch heuristics.

What this PR does (summary):
- Introduces primer_fabric: a configurable runner that composes synthetic "primers" from a small library of seed fragments. The fabric can emit sequences with controlled overlap, stagger, and interleaving to mimic realistic warm/cold handoffs.
- Adds a hotpath_attribution exporter that aggregates per-request kernel occupancy and attributes token-work to kernel-level flame points. Output is a compact NDJSON stream and a flamegraph-friendly folded file.
- Provides a small set of primer profiles (configs/primer_profiles.yaml) and an orchestration helper (scripts/collect_flame.sh) to run short experiments, collect perf samples, and upload to the benchdata bucket.
- CI bench job to run a lightweight fidelity check and smoke the exporter to ensure metrics schema compatibility.

Why this is different: primer_fabric focuses on mesh-like primer patterns (many short primers interleaved with occasional long pass-throughs) rather than single long warmups. The exporter maps kernel occupancy back to primer classes so teams can ask "which primer sequences trigger the slow kernel X" instead of just seeing aggregate p95 numbers.

Design notes and constraints:
- Memory footprint: runner keeps only a small sliding window of KV checkpoints to avoid high mem overhead when running many parallel primer strands.
- Sampling: exporter uses stochastic perf-sample sampling with adaptive backoff to avoid perturbing latency under high QPS.
- Determinism: primer fabric accepts a seed so runs can be replayed; profiles encode expected seq-length distribution and overlap ratio.

Commits (high level):

- bd1f7a8: add overlap/stagger controls and deterministic seeding
- f2e8a61: implement hotpath_attribution exporter and NDJSON schema

Changed areas (high level files):

Small illustrative diff (runner loop excerpt):

    request = primer.to_request()
    # attach ephemeral KV checkpoint for this strand (keeps <4 checkpoints by design)

    resp = client.call(request)
    exporter.observe(resp, primer.metadata)

CI and validation:
- Initial CI run failed due to a race in the perf-sample collector; fixed in c3d9f0e and re-ran.
- CI bench smoke job runs the runner with the "mesh" profile, validates NDJSON schema, and asserts folded flame output contains expected kernel names (approx 3 sample kernels in benchdata sample).
- Final CI status: pass (all checks green).

Review conversation (high level):
- Noah Chen (reviewer): "Can we make the checkpoint retention configurable? In our multi-tenant lab runs we might need to shrink further."
  - Author (Priya): "Added --max-checkpoints flag, default 4. Caller can reduce to 1 for tight memory runs."
- Sofia Ruiz (reviewer): "Exporter schema looks good; please add versioned schema header to NDJSON so we can evolve."
  - Author: "Added schema_version and a lightweight validator in hotpath_exporter; updated tests to assert version header."
- Raj Patel (reviewer): "Minor: rename 'mesh' profile to 'interleaved' to be clearer."
  - Author: "Renamed profile and left a compatibility alias to avoid breaking old job names."
- PR was squashed after approvals; maintainers ran a short cluster acceptance run on the canary bench cluster prior to merge.

Performance notes from bench runs:
- Mesh/interleaved profile ~ increased tail kernel occupancy by 12% compared to single-warmup baseline in our 30s runs.
- Prefetch probe sequences illuminated a small path where kernel X (cuda kernel 0x8f1) had a 9% higher SM contention when primers overlapped >60% (this is surfaced in the flame fold).
- Exporter introduces negligible overhead (sampled collection; <1% latency increase in smoke runs).

How to use:
- Quickstart: see README_primer_fabric.md. Example: ./scripts/collect_flame.sh --profile interleaved --seed 42 --duration 30s --out benchdata/myrun.folded
- Output: NDJSON lines with fields: timestamp, request_id, primer_class, kernel_map (flattened), and folded lines for flamegraph viewers.

Next work (follow-ups):
- Add a cross-run aggregator that correlates primer classes with model-level generation artifacts (ENG-4199).
- Integrate exporter outputs into the bench dashboard and add per-model drilldowns.

Merge: squashed and merged to main on 2024-11-20 after CI pass and approvals.

Contact: Priya Kothari (priya@redwood.example) for follow-ups and sample run reproduction steps.
